newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH GOVT STILL THINKS CAN HALVE UNEMPLOYMENT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH GOVT STILL THINKS CAN HALVE UNEMPLOYMENT.

text.p: The Finnish government's economic policy minister committee said in a statement on Tuesday it still thought it would be possible to halve the unemployment rate by 1999.
The committee, chaired by Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen, on Tuesday discussed a report on employment by a group of top-level civil servants.
"The committee thought that the results of the conducted economic and employment policies are now starting to show," it said.

"The strengthening of economic growth and the emphasis on this year of the effects of the employment programme make it possible that the target to halve unemployment can be reached," the committee added.
The government, in office since spring 1995, has stated that halving the unemployment rate to 8-9 percent by 1999 is its most important objective. Unemployment was 15.9 percent in November.
